content:
elaine: Hey @people-ops — planning to be in Spain for ~9 months starting June. Does that create a tax nexus? Also curious about WFH stipend continuation and pension/401k effects while abroad. Thanks!

nora-peopleops: Hi Elaine :wave: short answer: 9 months can trigger local tax/residency rules depending on country. Spain uses ~183-day rule — you could be considered a tax resident if you spend >183 days in a calendar year. Can you DM payroll the exact move dates?

elaine: Dates are 2026-06-01 to 2027-02-28. That's across two calendar years, so seems awkward. Do I need to change `home_base` in Rippling or submit a specific form? :thinking:

sam-payroll: @elaine please open this internal form: https://payroll.internal.company/relo-declare — we'll do a withholding/residency check. If you change `home_base` to Spain we need local address, passport copy, and equivalent tax ID. Payroll cutover usually takes 1-2 pay cycles after docs.

ben-legal: Quick flag: Spain may require social security registration if you're performing work there and are resident. Even if you stay on US payroll, local authorities may deem there is a permanent establishment/employer obligation depending on length and activities. We'll run a cross-border assessment once payroll has the dates.

marco-eng: Does this affect the WFH stipend? I'm budgeting for coworking and the stipend helps.

nora-peopleops: WFH stipend is country-adjusted. For temporary remote (<12 months) our standard is: continue stipend up to 6 months automatically; beyond 6 months we review on a case-by-case basis. For your 9-month plan we'll likely pro-rate monthly payments. Example (informal): `prorated = monthly_stipend * months_paid` — we'll confirm amounts.

elaine: Got it. Any impact on benefits like 401(k) / pension?

sam-payroll: Good q. If you become covered by Spanish social security, US 401(k) contributions may stop or be paused. Employer match depends on payroll location. We'll coordinate with Benefits to provide options.

jill-benefits: Hi all — if Elaine moves onto a local payroll and enrolls in Spanish social security, US retirement contributions (401k deferrals + match) will typically end. Spain has statutory pension contributions; we'll prepare a side-by-side estimate showing take-home diff. Please file the "international payroll review" ticket so Benefits + Payroll can sync.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: For moves >90 days, submit the Temporary Work Abroad form at least 14 days before departure: https://docs.company/temporary-work-abroad — failure to submit may delay stipend/benefits adjustments.

elaine: Thanks — I'll DM payroll and submit the form. Quick follow-up: am I still eligible for relocation stipend? This is temporary, not permanent.

nora-peopleops: Relocation stipend = for permanent relocations only. For temporary assignments we offer a "remote travel allowance" (one-time or monthly capped depending on length). For ~9 months we'd typically provide monthly allowance or coworking reimbursement with manager approval. Send receipts in Concur.

marco-eng: tagging manager @liz-manager to approve coworking costs while Elaine is abroad.

liz-manager: Approved for coworking up to $150/mo while Elaine is abroad — please confirm receipts monthly.

elaine: Awesome, thanks everyone :raised_hands: I'll start the forms and DM payroll with passport + dates. Appreciate the help!
